text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's second largest airport Billund is now the regional airport in western Denmark operating most flights to foreign destinations and thus participating fully in the ever escalating competition between airports in Europe, according to a report on their future by investment bank Salomon Brothers.

--- Danish toy group Lego's entertainment park, Legoland, in Windsor, west London reached its target of 1.4 million visitors in its first 1996 summer season. Next spring construction of a new Legoland begins in San Diego, California, for opening in 1999.

--- Denmark has demanded a prompt reply from Turkey on allegations against Turkish police of torturing a Danish citizen of Kurdish extraction, who was jailed last summer during a family visit to Ankara after being accused of being a member of the Kurdish PKK separatist organisation. The Turkish ambassador to Denmark dismisses the allegations as anti-Turkish propaganda.
--- Some 50 harbours run by Danish local authorities are demanding law reforms to allow them to operate as private limited companies, the aim being to increase competitiveness and attract investment.

--- Danish shareholders make much smaller profits than other European and U.S. investors due to the fact that Denmark's largest investors, the pension funds, insist on ploughing back large parts of their profits into their own companies.
